Strings.uninstallerEnableCaption: Runs an app’s own uninstaller, then finds the caches, settings, logs and other leftovers it leaves behind.
Strings.uninstallerStep1: Pick the app you want to remove from the list.
Strings.uninstallerStep2: Its own uninstaller runs first. That step can’t be undone.
Strings.uninstallerStep3: Review what it left behind. Files go to the Recycle Bin and registry entries are backed up first.
win.uninstaller.intro: Its own uninstaller runs first, which can’t be undone. Then you review what it left behind.
win.uninstaller.notTrusted: This app isn’t installed under Program Files or AppData\Local\Programs, so its leftovers can’t be told apart from other files. Only its uninstaller runs.
win.uninstaller.runningFormat: %@ is running. Close it before uninstalling.
win.uninstaller.forceQuitFormat: %@ ends immediately. Unsaved work in it is lost.
win.uninstaller.quietCaption: Uses the uninstaller’s silent mode when it has one. Some uninstallers still show a window.
win.uninstaller.adminNote: This app is installed for all users, so its uninstaller asks for administrator approval. To also remove its leftovers for all users, restart this app as administrator before you uninstall.
win.uninstaller.irreversibleNote: The app’s own uninstaller runs next. That step can’t be undone; what it leaves behind is reviewed afterwards.
win.uninstaller.confirmMessage: The app’s own uninstaller runs now and may ask questions or for administrator approval. This can’t be undone. Afterwards you review what it left behind before anything else is removed.
win.uninstaller.confirmRunning: The app is still running. Its uninstaller may ask you to close it.
win.uninstaller.startFailedFormat: The uninstaller could not be started: %@
win.uninstaller.waitingHint: Finish the steps in the uninstaller’s window. If it closed or you are done, click I’ve finished.
win.uninstaller.stillInstalledFormat: %@ is still installed. The uninstaller may have been cancelled or may need the PC to restart. Nothing else was removed.
win.uninstaller.registryAdminNote: Registry entries for all users need administrator rights, so they stay in place.
win.uninstaller.reviewNote: Scheduled tasks and services are listed for review only. Remove them in Task Scheduler or Services if you no longer need them.
win.uninstaller.relatedFormat: Found by the name “%@”. Check that it really belongs to this app.
win.uninstaller.removeMessageFormat: %1$d items (%2$@) go to the Recycle Bin.
win.uninstaller.removeRegistryNote: Registry entries can’t go to the Recycle Bin. Each one is saved to a .reg backup file first; opening that file restores it.
win.uninstaller.backupNote: Removed registry entries were saved to backup files. Open one to restore its entry.
Strings.uninstallerSelectionUnavailable: This app can’t be uninstalled from here. Choose another from the list.
